Set cim_report_detection_window to the longest lookback your correlation searches use.


Short Description:
Measure and validate Splunk CIM compliance at the data model and dataset level — with field-mapping quality scoring, unmapped data discovery, prescribed-value validation, remediation priorities, data model testing, TA sourcetype coverage and inventory, and automated reporting.


Description:
The CIM Assessment Toolkit (CAT) measures and validates Common Information Model (CIM) compliance across your Splunk data models at the data model + dataset level. CAT scores field-mapping quality, data quality, and prescribed-value compliance; surfaces unmapped sourcetypes and impact-ranked remediation priorities; monitors data model acceleration health; and generates professional Word-document reports with optional scheduled email delivery. A new feature is four TA Inventory tables which reveal what TAs cover which sourcetypes for CIM normalization and their versions - essential information for maintaining CIM normalization coverage. To reduce CIM Assessment Report length, detailed field gaps, mapped & unmapped sourcetypes, and installed Splunk apps lists are attached as CSVs (CIM_Field_Gaps_*, CIM_Mapped_Sourcetypes_*, Splunk_Installed_Apps_*) to the report email.

item.title: Hurricane Labs Add-on for Windows PowerShell Transcript - v0.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\## 0.2.0 Tested on Splunk Enterprise 9.4.3, 10.4.1 and 10.6.1. Supports Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.x transcripts. \### Fixes \- Events are now timestamped with the session's Start time instead of the transcript file's last-modified time. \- PowerShell 7 transcripts ("PowerShell transcript start") now split into one event per session, and their end blocks are dropped. CRLF and LF files both work. \- Transcripts in other languages now parse: Windows PowerShell 5.1 on non-English Windows and PowerShell 7.6.6+ translate the header, so parsing now goes by the header's layout instead of English words. \- user, domain, username, runas_user and runas_domain keep dots, spaces and $ in names, and handle NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. \- std_out now starts after the header for both PowerShell versions. \- computer/dest no longer spans several lines when the machine name is blank. \### Eventtype changes (search time) \- powershell_encoded_command matches every -EncodedCommand abbreviation (-e, -ec, -enc ...) and the / forms (/e, /enc ...), but only when followed by a base64 UTF-16LE payload. -Encoding abbreviations and other tools' -e (docker, git, sed) no longer match. \- powershell_command needs -Command (or -c, -com ...) on a line that runs powershell or pwsh. -ComputerName, -ComObject, Invoke-Command, Get-Command, python -c and bash -c no longer match. \- powershell_nslookup_txt also matches -type\=txt and -querytype\=txt. \- powershell_registry also matches Get-ItemProperty -Path HK... and Set-Location HK... \### New \- CIM Endpoint.Processes field names: dest, process, process_id, process_path, process_name, action. \- powershell_transcript_session eventtype for opting in to the CIM Endpoint data model (no data model tags by default; see the README). \- Splunk Cloud readiness: \[id] stanza in app.conf and sc_admin write access. \### Upgrade notes \- Timestamp, line-breaking and end-block changes apply only to newly indexed data. \- Eventtype changes apply at search time, so they change what existing saved searches and alerts on these eventtypes match. \- Events are now dated by session start, which can be well before Splunk receives them. Scheduled searches with short lookbacks should search by arrival time, e.g. \_index_earliest\=-20m. \- Transcript times have no time zone. A single forwarder reading transcripts from several time zones needs a per-host TZ (see the README). \### Known limitations \- A session is one event, and Splunk drops everything past 256 KB (TRUNCATE), so commands after very long output aren't indexed. \- Command output that reproduces a transcript header (e.g. Get-Content of another transcript) splits the session there, and later commands take that header's fields and start time. \- Full list in the README.


Description:
This app provides knowledge objects for working with Windows PowerShell transcript logs. In addition to field extractions, a number of event types are included to support threat hunting use cases. You will need to configure your Windows systems to log PowerShell transcripts in order to benefit from this app. This logging is not enabled by default in Windows. These logs, once generated, should be collected via a file input and forwarded to Splunk. Additional information on the configuration of this app is available here: www.hurricanelabs.com/splunk-tutorials/splunk-tutorial-powershell-transcription-logging This app is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/HurricaneLabs/TA-powershell_transcript

item.title: Eventgen Manager - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Eventgen Manager 2.0.0 generates events itself. SA-Eventgen is no longer required. NEW Built-in generation engine (eventgen_manager_engine modular input). Pure Python, runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows, on x86 and ARM. Configuration changes apply within seconds. No restart needed. Send test events from the editor to the real destination without turning the configuration on. Live status per configuration: state, events generated, last batch, and the reason for any failure. Automatic timestamps, with a new "Timestamp to write" option: generated time, or current time for testing detections that search the last few minutes. New random values: weighted, ipv4private, email, useragent, uuid. New seqfile replacement. Rated replacements now work. Counters continue from their last value after a restart. verifySSL setting for HEC and Splunk REST receivers. Rebuilt Throughput dashboard: events per second, projected daily volume, failed batches, and configured against measured rates. New Tutorial page with a complete, step-by-step guide. The engine can also run from the command line, outside Splunk. UPGRADING FROM SA-EVENTGEN Existing eventgen.conf configurations work unchanged. If SA-Eventgen is running, the built-in engine waits on standby so events are not doubled. Use "Switch to the built-in engine" on the Generator control page. CHANGED Syslog output now uses TCP. UDP output is removed, as UDP is not allowed on Splunk Cloud or under app certification. To send to indexers over splunktcp, keep the output on modinput and set up forwarding in outputs.conf on the instance running the app. Settings that only tuned SA-Eventgen's worker pools, plugins, and templates are removed from the editor. Existing values are kept in eventgen.conf. FIXED The structured application log starter wrote local time with a "Z" (UTC) suffix. It now sets timezone \= 0000. Tutorial: [https://github.com/genai-telemetry/eventgen-manager/blob/main/Eventgen_Manager_Tutorial.pdf](https://github.com/genai-telemetry/eventgen-manager/blob/main/Eventgen_Manager_Tutorial.pdf)


Short Description:
Configure, preview, and generate realistic test data in Splunk from the browser. A built-in engine runs eventgen.conf configurations directly, with a guided editor, live preview, and throughput monitoring.


Description:
Eventgen Manager configures, previews, and generates realistic test data in Splunk from the browser. Since version 2.0 it includes its own generation engine, so SA-Eventgen is no longer required, and existing eventgen.conf configurations run unchanged. A guided editor covers the eventgen.conf settings, so you never hand-edit the file. Pick a sample file, set how often and how many events to send, choose what to replace in each line, and watch a live preview with every generated value highlighted before anything reaches an index. Send test events to the real destination with one click to confirm the index, sourcetype, and output are right. The built-in engine is pure Python and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows, on x86 and ARM. Changes apply within seconds with no restart. Output goes to the local index, HTTP Event Collector, Splunk REST, files, spool folders, raw TCP, or syslog over TCP. On a heavy forwarder, events are forwarded to your indexers through outputs.conf. Use it for demos, dashboard development, detection and alert testing, training, and load testing. A Throughput dashboard shows events per second, projected daily volume, failed batches, and configured against measured rates.

Short Description:

Description:
Inno AI Report attaches an "AI Situation Analysis" tab to a Splunk dashboard you already have. When a user presses the button, the app collects the results that are currently on screen, summarises them, and asks your Splunk AI Toolkit connection to interpret them together. The report gives a status grade (Normal / Warning / Critical / Undetermined), a panel-by-panel reading, ranked cause hypotheses with supporting and contradicting evidence, recommended actions with the responsible team, impact scope and urgency, and the data gaps that limited the analysis. It does not need to know what your dashboard searches do. Panel results are generalised into field=value lines without depending on particular field names, so the app attaches to dashboards it has never seen. A wizard does the work: pick an app and a dashboard, choose the business domain and the report language, press one button. The original dashboard is backed up automatically and can be restored from the same wizard. Six business-domain presets (network, security, infrastructure, application, business and general) change the analyst role, what is cited as evidence, which team is named in each action, and how to verify. Reports can be produced in Korean, English or Japanese. Nothing is sent to the vendor. The model runs wherever your AI Toolkit connection points, and the app calls it only when a user presses the button, so a dashboard carrying the tab costs nothing until it is used. Generated analysis can be wrong or incomplete. It is meant to support operational decisions, not to replace them. More from inno software: Inno AI Chat lets you ask the follow-up question in plain language, and Inno Observability brings multi-vendor network, infrastructure, application and database monitoring, log anomaly detection and eBPF tracing onto your on-premises Splunk platform. See the Details tab.

item.title: Cisco DC Networking - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
* Added column sorting throughout product details, related objects, endpoint/path evidence, exact measurements, lifecycle, checkpoint and setup tables, including separate interface Admin and Operational states. Activate a column heading again to reverse direction. Sorting applies to all loaded matching rows before pagination; it does not request extra controller data. Numeric zero remains a value, missing values sort last, and action-only columns remain controls. * Corrected proxy credential URL encoding across product connections, preserving spaces and special characters in outbound authentication while retaining saved account settings. * Improved ACI physical-interface status, units and operational-speed presentation, and connected Overview switch details to the existing Inventory investigations without adding controller requests. * Connected consecutive reported measurements in shared time-series charts regardless of sample spacing. Preserved actual sample markers, series identity, exact values and keyboard selection; missing values are not filled or interpreted as zero. * ACI health and active-fault reads finish when APIC's validated page total proves completion, avoiding a redundant empty request. Changed child populations restart only the pending parent probe; written-page recovery and controller budgets remain intact. * Contract consumer/provider relationships correlate on the observed contract parent DN without assuming a reverse-relation name format. Routing views label node/VRF-sharing L3Outs as configuration context rather than implying a unique peer association. * Endpoint attachment history compares interfaces within each observed node; vPC peer observations are not labelled as endpoint moves. Cross-node migration requires separate source evidence. * Normally completed, count-verified searches accept Splunk's exact reduced-bucket performance notice. Truncation, unknown warnings and abnormal jobs still fail closed. * ACI history classes interrupted by a read timeout yield the next branch turn while retaining checkpoints, controller cooldowns and request limits. * Authentication views exclude collector credential metadata. Learned MAC observations no longer appear as IP addresses through CIM aliases, and zero-result messages apply to both text and field filters. * Fault Type filters retain APIC’s native type from vendor metadata or original JSON instead of Splunk’s normalized event classification. * Corrected ACI tenant/EPG counts to use canonical policy identities, reconciled active faults with indexed faultInst evidence, and added native Severity/Domain/Type filters. ACI views use contextual row actions and account labels while preserving controller identifiers. * Added physical fabricLink topology with observed ports, IP/MAC endpoint search, system-model correlation and per-site firmware distribution. New indexed investigations cover external EPG subnets, contract consumers/providers, node hardware, BGP/OSPF neighbors and PBR/IP SLA evidence. Optional collection stays explicit and missing operational telemetry stays unknown. * ND partial resource batches now include acknowledged output in cycle event totals while retaining incomplete status and resume checkpoints. * Connectivity Analysis now distinguishes authentication timeouts, TLS failures, connection failures and rejected logins from fabric API failures, including errors wrapped by the shared ND login client. Diagnostics never expose credentials or controller response bodies. * Made ND policy retirement reachable from Setup’s disabled-input list and account-deletion guidance. Review reads local retirement evidence without reconnecting every configured controller. Accounts may be removed after a directly created policy’s full retirement proof is verified; disabled safety records and permanent fences remain. Ordinary disabled policies, MDS references and protected migration recovery remain guarded. * Clarified that ND discovery creates related ACI/Nexus 9000 accounts, lists their identities and explains incomplete discovery sources. Search scope retains explicit monitoring destinations before first events and when indexed-data discovery fails, and includes reduced buckets in index discovery. * Fixed the narrow Connectivity Analysis wrapper, switched fabric discovery to the documented inventory summary and added safe connection-error categories. ND IP cells link to scoped Endpoint Search; hosted/outbound protocol values display names and numbers. Traffic categories compare the latest service-list collection against the latest ND summary and explain count mismatches without inventing rates or collection-health failures. * Corrected MDS direct syslog header/timestamp recognition for colon-prefixed messages without a hostname, including optional process text. MDS severity lookups now return one canonical value. Added the SSH/terminal procedure used for a real UDP receiver test, with CFS isolation, verbosity and restoration guidance. New timestamp assignment requires receiver activation; historical event times are unchanged and MDS TLS remains separately unverified. * Expanded MDS syslog setup with destination-capacity checks, isolated test and restoration steps, receipt-time searches and packet-level troubleshooting. Added Mac/VPN receiver instructions covering address changes, TLS identity and cleanup; live MDS delivery and mutual TLS remain separate qualification checks. * Protected new ACI events from reserved metadata collisions by preserving device attributes such as index\=1, 2 or 3 under vendor-prefixed names. Historical JSON index attributes remain available as vendor_index. Removed the global calculated index field because it can suppress exact-sourcetype event retrieval even when indexed counts are present. Existing raw data is unchanged; historical records can still expose vendor index values during automatic extraction. Use an explicit, search-local bucket-derived display field when investigating those older records; do not redefine the reserved index field globally. * Fixed Complete MDS monitoring setup rejecting valid end-port inventories above 1,000 records. The bounded readiness check now allows up to 50,000 records and tests the zones endpoint separately from VSAN inventory. Zoning pagination now follows the configured record limit instead of stopping at 10,000 records, and validates NDFC page-range metadata. Limited coverage is shown before creation; independent zoning feeds continue when another feed fails, with degraded health and the previous complete-success checkpoint preserved. * Fixed MDS monitoring setup rejecting the supported aggregate-alarm fallback. Readiness now shows all ten datasets and their blocking reasons, distinguishes safety-limit failures from unsupported response formats, and explains how to select a supported subset without weakening collection checks. * Clarified Nexus Dashboard, including Nexus Dashboard SAN, ACI, Nexus 9000 switch and MDS switch collection paths. Corrected automatic account-discovery guidance, documented blank credentials and retry behavior, and separated account associations from overlapping dataset collection. Direct MDS API collection remains unavailable; existing NDFC SAN collection and independent MDS syslog are unchanged. * Made Syslog & audit navigation consistent across Nexus Dashboard, ACI, Nexus 9000 and MDS. Added an independent MDS workspace with full-window counts, recent switch messages, Fibre Channel context, configuration and authentication evidence, and receiver setup links. Existing ACI and Nexus 9000 section URLs remain compatible; MDS live sender validation remains separate. * Corrected direct ACI syslog header, fault/event and ACL packet fields, including nested affected-object paths and sender timestamp recognition. Added streamed ACL investigation and expanded Nexus 9000 Syslog & audit with all messages and authentication history. Quiet streams no longer appear stale; classic Nexus charts now count before display limits and retain native message/host/time fallbacks. Syslog Coverage avoids unrelated API checks while retaining separate indexed-delivery and receiver evidence. Syslog investigation dialogs no longer infer controller links or API scope from sender names. * Fixed enable and disable controls for TLS syslog listeners on Home and Configured Inputs. The event-volume chart now shows exact product and bucket values on hover or keyboard focus, abbreviates large display values, and opens each segment in Splunk Search. * Added a normalized collector-cycle runtime contract with status, duration, API-call, event, dataset, warning, and checkpoint evidence where the collector can prove those values. * Added sanitized ownership heartbeats with product, input, owner, and installed version/build identity without presenting a heartbeat as proof that the upstream product API is healthy. * Moved app-owned file logs under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/cisco_dc_networking/` while retaining recursive `_internal` visibility. ##### Search, event, and compatibility contracts * Added administrator-controlled search-scope macros for each product and a guarded **Search Scope & Acceleration** editor for destination indexes and `summariesonly` behavior. * Fixed shared search macros so Classic dashboards, saved searches, data models, and React drilldowns remain valid in generating-command, nested-search, and inline search contexts. * Normalized controller identity across Nexus Dashboard, ACI, and Nexus 9000 API events. Incomplete responses are rejected instead of displaying a partial list. * Declares affected-node fields as multivalue in the Nexus Dashboard Anomalies and Advisories data-model datasets, preserving the source node arrays. * Corrects the managed Flow worker to use the controller-version API contract, preserves unified statistics through historical field aliases, honors server-capped pagination, and bounds repeated connection or service failures while retaining failed windows for retry. * Extends the Health, Systems, Statistics, and Nexus Dashboard data models with controller addresses, container/process metrics, and Orchestrator fields. Bounded ordered requests, a five-minute identity overlap, and visible checkpoint failures replace controller-clock progress and silent failures. * Added observation timestamps and resumable page progress for current ACI health and active faults. Historical records use their original creation time; unchanged health observations remain available on later polls. Interrupted uncommitted pages and the first legacy overlap can still replay records. * Preserved original historical checkpoint identities during protected ACI plan consolidation and backout. Replacement plans retain the original keys and ownership locks; missing receipts, mapping drift, or pre-existing independent replacement checkpoints require review. * Fixed Nexus 9000 neighbor topology, multi-command component ownership, DME query validation, and grouped exact-class selection. * Fixed MDS/NDFC authentication reporting, fabric identity, SAN Analytics fabric recovery, inventory readiness, policy editing, congestion ingestion, and bounded alarm degradation reporting. * Fixed Nexus Dashboard Orchestrator serialization, software-history event shaping, migration continuity, Congestion review layout, recovery-row visibility, and retirement performance. * Fixed Nexus Dashboard fabric discovery so events without `fabricName` do not create a selectable **Null** command-center filter. * Fixed dashboard search macro regressions, ACI `tstats` host filtering, bucketed timecharts, source-type parsing, event-type index scope, saved-search thresholds, and lookup contracts. * Fixed default-input provisioning, account-dependent form states, proxy toggles, field resets, product icon routing, action alignment, responsive wrapping, and configured-input grouping. ##### Upgrade and compatibility notes * Back up the current app, local configuration, encrypted credentials, and app-owned KV Store collections before installing 2.0.0. A migration restore point protects one transaction and is not a replacement for that backup. * Install the App and Technical Add-on as one versioned package. A restore point is saved before disabled staging, existing work finishes before replacement activation, and recovery continues after closing the browser or restarting Splunk. Previous exact-preservation migration receipts remain under **Review previous protected migration**; **Review or repair setup** remains available for protected recovery. * Keep retained pre-upgrade inputs and the downloaded export through the operational soak and recovery window. Create and test the required connection before creating a policy. * Review field-based searches that parse ACI or Orchestrator `_raw` punctuation. Named-field searches remain compatible across retained and new event formats. * Review product search-scope macros when data is stored outside the factory index scope. Review data-model acceleration before enabling `summariesonly`. * Restart during an approved maintenance window before the first Nexus Dashboard automatic handover after installation. The workflow checks that earlier workers have exited before relying on the installed drain guards. Other restart requirements reported by Splunk remain separate. * Already indexed events are not removed by migration backout, policy retirement, old-input cleanup, or configuration downgrade. ##### Supported boundaries and known limitations * Automatic handover requires proven app-owned local inputs on a supported standalone or heavy-forwarder collection instance with Unix file locks. Restoring previous monitoring can replay data collected since the handover. * Two fresh collection cycles establish replacement startup. Partial collection errors remain visible as degraded startup and a collection-health follow-up; they are not described as healthy or fully indexed. A failed startup or verification timeout restores original input states. One small INFO cycle audit is emitted even when ordinary diagnostics use an error-only level, without changing that configured level. * ACI and Nexus 9000 support first-class API collection plus externally delivered syslog. SNMP, gNMI/model-driven telemetry, NetFlow, and APIC WebSocket subscriptions remain optional external integrations. * MDS and SAN Analytics collection uses qualified NDFC SAN APIs; this release does not add direct standalone MDS switch collection or configure SAN Analytics on NDFC. * Hyperfabric and MDS managed policies must run on one active collection owner. Local overlap protection does not coordinate independently enabled copies across hosts. * Custom API discovery shows GET operations or object classes advertised by the selected controller. Hyperfabric uses the current official cloud API publication. Availability depends on permissions, enabled services, and supported response/pagination contracts; missing or incomplete metadata is reported explicitly. * Generated Dashboard Studio views are retained only as migration references and are not promoted as supported replacements for the established Classic dashboards.


Description:
The Cisco Data Center Networking App delivers a comprehensive solution for data onboarding and visualization tailored to Cisco Data Center Networking products, including Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches, Cisco ACI, and Cisco Nexus Dashboard. Data collection is achieved through APIs. Key features of the app include: Simplified Data Onboarding: Leveraging the Splunk UCC framework and default input selection, the app streamlines the process of integrating data into Splunk. It also enhances cross-correlation capabilities across data platforms by utilizing a unified index and application structure. Centralized Monitoring: Offers real-time monitoring of Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches, Cisco ACI fabrics, and Cisco Nexus Dashboard, providing detailed insights into anomalies and advisories with specific information about affected network objects. Customizable Dashboards: Includes a default dashboard optimized for faster loading using Base Search. Additionally, users can create personalized views to meet their specific requirements, ensuring critical data is easily accessible.

item.title: Jamf Pro Add-on - v3.0.4 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
# Jamf Pro Add-on for Splunk — Changelog *** ## Version 3.0.4 > **Compatibility Note:** This release requires Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform **10.2 or later** (i.e., Splunk versions that support the Python 3.13 interpreter.) > > Jamf is no longer publishing a Python 3.9-compatible version of this add-on via Splunkbase. Python 3.9 is end of life and continued support would require the inclusion of Python packages that have unpatched vulnerabilities and outdated cryptography libraries. Additionally, Splunk Cloud 10.6 drops 3.9 support entirely and the current version of Splunk AppInspect will not permit Splunkbase release of add-ons pinned to Python 3.9. If your Splunk environment only has Python 3.9 available, you'll need to upgrade Splunk before installing this or future versions of the add-on. Please contact Jamf Support if you are unable to update to a modern version of Splunk. ### Updates The only change is moving the Computer Inventory input from the `v1/computers-inventory` Jamf Pro API endpoint to the more modern /v4 endpoint. The structure of the JSON data returned by the v1 and v4 endpoints is similar so most reports and queries should continue to work without change, with one notable exception — the date-time when a device last contacted Jamf Pro. * /v1: `general.lastContactTime` * /v4: `general.lastContact` We felt it would be confusing if we patched a key to something other than what the API documents to maintain backwards compatibility. Therefore, we've chosen to store this key as the Jamf Pro API provides it. As a result, if you have queries that reference this key, update them to use the new key name. If you have a time-series analysis that looks at a computer's records over time that references this key, use the coalesce function to ensure that your query works no matter which API version sourced the event: `| eval last_contact \= coalesce('general.lastContact', 'general.lastContactTime')` *** ## Version 3.0.3 ### Bugs Fixed * **JSON fields from Computer and Mobile Device inventory are now extracted and searchable.** Events from the Computer Inventory and Mobile Device Inventory inputs are indexed as JSON, but their sourcetypes were configured so Splunk performed no field extraction — the raw event was visible in search results, yet individual fields (e.g. computer name, hardware, operating system, extension attributes) could not be searched, filtered, or reported on. All `jssUapiComputer:*` and `jssMobileDevice:*` sourcetypes now use JSON key-value mode, so their fields are parsed automatically. This is a search-time change, so fields are also extracted from events that were already indexed before the upgrade — no re-indexing is required. ### Maintenance * The add-on version is now defined in a single place (`globalConfig.json`) and propagated to every other file (app metadata, package, and the Jamf Pro User-Agent) at build time, so the reported version can no longer drift between them. *** ## Version 3.0.0 Version 3 is a major release. **The accompanying** [**Upgrade Guide**](Splunk-Add-On-for-Jamf%20Pro_v3-Upgrade-Guide.md) **should be reviewed before installing this version.** ### Splunk Version Compatibility * Migrated from Splunk Add-on Builder (AOB) to the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) framework. * Upgraded Python runtime from 3.9 to 3.13. All bundled packages are now resolved at build time against Python 3.13, replacing cp39 compiled extensions that could not load under Splunk Enterprise 10.2. ### New Features * **Account-driven credentials.** Jamf Pro URL, username/client ID, and password/secret are now configured once on a separate Account settings section and referenced by name from each input. Create, edit, and test accounts on the new **Configuration → Accounts** tab. * **In-place upgrade from v2.12.x.** On first run after upgrade, the add-on automatically migrates each existing input into the new account-driven model. * **Test Credentials button** on the Account form. Probes the Jamf Pro instance with entered credentials and returns verified/invalid/error feedback before save. Enforces HTTPS and rejects private/reserved/metadata IP ranges (SSRF protection). * **Explicit Authentication type dropdown** on the Account form (`API Client` or `Username + Password`). Replaces the 2.x convention of prefixing the username with `client:`; accounts upgraded from 2.x are auto-corrected on first run. * **Test Endpoint button** on the Custom API Query input form. Probes the configured endpoint against stored credentials before save, so typos are caught at edit time rather than via silent post-save failure. * `skip_unchanged` checkpointing on Computer and Mobile Device inputs. The add-on remembers each record's content hash between polls and suppresses events for records whose payload is byte-identical to the last fetched copy. * **Unified input error reporting.** Every operator-actionable failure from any input writes an event to both the add-on's input log and a searchable `sourcetype=jamf:input:error` index event. Each event carries a `category` field — `config`, `auth`, `endpoint`, or `record` — for filtering and alerting. * **Event time format** option on the Computer Inventory input: choose between time of import, last inventory update, or last contact time. * **Auth Type column** in the Accounts table shows "API Client" or "User Account" at a glance. * Daily polling (86400 seconds) is now the default interval for all three inputs. ### Security * To guard against proxy-in-the-middle attacks, TLS certificate validation is now enforced on all connections to Jamf Pro. If your Jamf Pro server still uses a self-signed or private CA certificate, either update your Jamf Pro to use a publicly-trusted certificate or install your private certificate authority's trust chain in your Splunk server's CA-Cert store before upgrading. ### Bugs Fixed * Many errors arising from incorrectly-configured inputs have been remediated. Error handling and logging have been modernized across the add-on.

\# Log Monitoring 3.15.0 This release is for upgrades from 3.12.2. It also contains 3.13.0, 3.14.0 and 3.14.1, which were not published separately. \## New \*\*Bulk actions on Log Outage\*\* \- A new Select column at the start of the table. Tick rows one by one, or use Select this page. \- Bulk action applies one action to all selected rows: Delete alert, Undo delete alert, Passive alert, Change threshold, Clear threshold override, Disable monitor or Re-enable monitor. \- Each action is applied only to the rows where the row menu would offer it. Before anything is saved, the dialog lists those rows and counts the ones it skips. Afterwards it reports how many rows changed, and lists any row that did not change, with the reason. \- Up to 200 rows at a time. Disable monitor, and any action on more than 20 rows, asks you to type the number of rows to confirm. \- After a bulk action, Undo puts the rows back as they were. It does not touch a row that someone has changed since. Undo is available until the page is reloaded. \*\*Admin Guide page\*\* \- A new page in the menu for the tasks that are done in the lookup files: stopping monitoring of an index, a sourcetype or a host. \- For each task it shows which lookup file to edit, the exact row to add, what happens, and how to undo it. \- It also lists everything that is stopped right now, read from those lookup files. A suppression that has no effect, because its reason is empty or its date cannot be read, is marked NOT ACTIVE. \- The page only reads; it changes nothing. \## Changed \- The Collector runs every 3 minutes instead of every 5. It still looks back 8 minutes, so one missed run leaves no gap. If you have set your own schedule for this search, yours is kept. \- New installs use a 4-hour outage threshold for all sources. Before, it was 24 hours, and 1 week for syslog sources. Existing installs keep the values in their \`dvlm_settings.csv\`. An empty value now falls back to 4 hours. \- The Index lists on Log Outage and Stream Health no longer show indexes set to \`off\`. \## Fixed \- Setting an index to \`off\` in \`dvlm_index_config.csv\` used to stop only data collection. The sources already tracked for that index stayed on the pages and turned Critical. They no longer appear as outages and raise no alerts. Their old rows stay in the collection until Maintenance Purge removes them. \## Upgrade 1\. Install over the existing app. The package contains no lookup files, so your lookups and decisions are kept. 2\. Optional: to use the 4-hour default, set \`default_threshold_sec\` and \`syslog_threshold_sec\` to 14400 in \`dvlm_settings.csv\`. 3\. If Log Outage does not show the Select column, reload the page without the browser cache. No saved searches, lookups, KV fields or permissions were added or removed. \## Known limitations Unchanged since 3.12. See README.txt. \## Rollback Reinstall 3.12.2. Your lookups and decisions are kept.


Short Description:
Detects log delivery outages per index/sourcetype/host by tracking arrival time and diagnosing whether the forwarder agent or source stopped delivering.


Description:
Log Monitoring detects log delivery outages on a per-index, per-sourcetype, per-host basis by tracking arrival time and diagnosing whether the forwarder agent or the source itself has stopped delivering data. The app uses scheduled searches to record the most recent arrival time for each source every five minutes and computes outage status at read time, eliminating the need for manual inventory maintenance. Detection is based on arrival time rather than event time to avoid false positives caused by clock skew or timestamp parsing failures. The app distinguishes between three failure modes: an agent that has stopped running, an agent that is running but not forwarding data, and a source that has genuinely stopped producing logs. This diagnosis relies on independent liveness signals from Splunk internal logs and deployment server phone-home data. All tracking data is stored in KV store collections and CSV lookups, with no custom indexes, Python code, scripted inputs, or custom commands required.

Release Notes:
Initial release. - Sourcetype and host trackers (every 15 minutes, tstats only) with KV store state, plus nightly arrival-gap and hour-of-week volume baselines. - Statuses: SILENT, LATE, FUTURE, LOW_VOLUME and HIGH_VOLUME, with seasonality-aware silence detection. - Dashboards: Overview, Entity Detail, Hosts, Data Quality, Manage and Help. - Four alerts (shipped disabled, no actions) that respect mutes and priority. - Tested on Splunk Enterprise 10.6.


Short Description:
Know when a data source goes quiet: silent sources and hosts, ingestion lag, timestamp problems and volume anomalies, with per-source learned baselines. No setup needed, Splunk Cloud compatible.


Description:
The first time anyone notices that a firewall, an endpoint agent or a cloud feed has stopped sending data is usually the day an investigation needs it. Data Source Watchdog catches that within minutes. Install it on your search head and you are done: no lookups to fill in and no thresholds to guess. Every 15 minutes a lightweight tstats tracker records when each index + sourcetype and each host last delivered data. Every night the app learns what normal looks like for each source - how long its gaps usually are and how many events it sends in each hour of the week. Each source is then flagged as SILENT (no data for longer than its own learned gap, seasonality-aware so business-hours sources do not alarm every night), LATE (ingestion lag above your threshold), FUTURE (events timestamped ahead of now), or LOW_VOLUME / HIGH_VOLUME compared with the same hour in previous weeks. The app also shows silent hosts and forwarders, timestamp-parsing and line-truncation problems per sourcetype with the props.conf fix to apply, a form to mute sources or set priorities and owners, and four ready-made alerts. It is pure SPL and Splunk Cloud compatible: no Python, no custom JavaScript, no inputs and no network calls.

Description:
HoneyLabs Intelligence is a free Splunk app for honeypot threat intelligence. It enriches the IP addresses in your own events with what HoneyLabs honeypot sensors recorded from them, indexes free threat feeds of active exploiter IP addresses and malware download URLs, and queries the honeypot dataset by port, payload, CVE, network, and JA4, Akin or HASSH fingerprint. HoneyLabs runs honeypot sensors on the public internet. No real user has a reason to connect to them, so the traffic they record comes from scanners, brute-force tools and exploit attempts looking for exposed systems. An address reaches the exploiter feed only when a sensor captured it running an exploit or a loader command, and known research scanners are left out. Every indicator links to its evidence at honeylabs.net/lookup. Getting started needs no account. Open the app's Setup page and turn on the threat feeds with one click each. Each feed is pulled every hour and needs no API key. The Triage dashboard then matches your traffic against them and lists hosts in your network that contacted captured malware infrastructure, followed by inbound connections from addresses seen running exploits. The honeylabs command enriches any event that carries a public IPv4 address: index=firewall | honeylabs field=src_ip | where honeylabs_events > 0 It adds a verdict, first and last seen, country, ASN and network owner, reverse DNS, the ports the address targeted and its exploit hits, each field prefixed honeylabs_. Addresses are de-duplicated per search, so a scanner that appears in ten thousand events costs one lookup. The honeylabssearch command queries the honeypot dataset directly. Its modes cover raw sensor events, captured request payloads, top attackers, timelines, IP, CIDR and domain lookups, CVE exploitation, ASN profiles, and fingerprint activity and population. Use it to see who else probes a CVE, what payload they send, or which sources share a JA4 fingerprint. The feeds and enrichment work without an account, and anonymous enrichment allows 10 lookups a day. A free API key from honeylabs.net raises that to 500 credits a day and is required for honeylabssearch and the Explorer dashboard. Pro allows 50,000 credits a day and Team 500,000. The key is stored through Splunk's storage/passwords, encrypted at rest and never written to a .conf file. A lookup sends only the public IP addresses in the field you name. Private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are filtered out before the request is built, and no other part of the event leaves your deployment. The feed inputs are plain HTTPS downloads and send nothing about your data. With Splunk Enterprise Security, load the same feeds through the ES threat intelligence framework so indicators reach correlation searches and risk scoring. The guide at honeylabs.net/integrations/splunk-es has the field mappings.

Description:
TA-IPMI is a free, source-available Splunk add-on that brings out-of-band hardware health monitoring to any Splunk host with a server-class BMC. It reads full IPMI telemetry via ipmitool's local open interface and indexes it three ways with zero manual configuration: 1. Sensor readings: every SDR sensor (temperatures, fan RPM, voltages such as 12V/3.3V/Vcore/BAT, power draw in watts, plus thresholds), plus chassis and BMC status as rich JSON events (index=main, sourcetype ipmi:status) for fielded search. 2. The same readings as time-series metrics in index=metrics (sourcetype ipmi:metrics, ipmi.* measure names), so thermal, fan, voltage and power trends survive retention and answer in milliseconds with mstats. 3. The System Event Log (SEL): each SEL record indexed exactly once as a separate event with sensor, event type, assertion state and raw detail preserved, so BIOS-level crashes, power faults, ECC errors, fan failures and intrusion alerts become searchable Splunk events. Why it matters: IPMI/BMC is the only observability layer that survives OS crashes, power loss, and hangs. Overheating servers, dead fans, failing PSUs, dropped redundancy and unexpected reboots happen below the OS where agents and syslog can't follow, but the BMC remembers everything. TA-IPMI closes that blind spot in minutes: install it on the host, and its BMC telemetry flows into Splunk with ready-made overview and trend dashboards.
